summary: PARTIAL is right. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) passes --max-semi-space-size=16 to the packaged desktop backend (both the early and the main-bundle spawn) and to the launchd/systemd units, as a runtime argument rather than through NODE_OPTIONS. Bun and dev get no flag, and tests cover all of this. Still open: (a) any server started through the CLI entry runs with the default: foreground `ryco`, `ryco start`, `ryco serve`, `npx ryco-cli`, and also the Desktop's SSH-managed remote server, which the auditor missed; (b) there is no streaming-load or GC benchmark, and the perf harness itself spawns the server without the flag. Probes run here: Electron 44.7 in node mode does honor the flag, but its default new space is 64 MiB, not 128 MiB, so the desktop saving is smaller than the plain-Node ~50 MiB. Setting the flag at runtime with v8.setFlagsFromString has no effect, so the CLI fix has to be a start-up flag: a process.execve re-exec, which cost about 27 ms here, or documentation.

evidence.note: DESKTOP_BACKEND_V8_FLAGS = ["--max-semi-space-size=16"]; desktopBackendSpawnArgs (:32-54) puts it first, only when nodeRuntime is true
early packaged backend spawn: nodeRuntime: true, so it gets the flag
launchBackendChild uses the same helper with nodeRuntime = !isDevelopment, so dev Bun gets no flag
Tests assert the flag in Node mode and no flags for Bun

NODE_SERVICE_V8_FLAGS and nodeServiceRuntimeArgs, gated on an execPath basename of node/nodeN/node.exe; nodeServiceCommand feeds both the plist ProgramArguments (:112) and the systemd ExecStart (:155)
The service spec uses process.execPath, which is the real node binary under Homebrew, nvm, volta and current Debian, so the basename gate is fine

The CLI entry only calls enableCompileCacheBestEffort(), then imports cliMain at :74-80. No flag check or re-exec, so foreground ryco/start/serve and npx run with the 128 MiB default (the auditor cited :36, which is the externalMcpArgs line)
MISSED BY AUDITOR: the Desktop's SSH remote runner execs `node $RYCO_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH` (dev only), then `ryco`, `npx --yes ryco-cli@...` or `npm exec`. None of them passes the flag
nohup launches a long-lived `serve` on the remote host through that runner. This is a Ryco-controlled long-lived backend without the cap

The perf harness spawns `node bin.mjs serve` without the flag, so lifecycle RSS numbers don't reflect the shipped desktop/service setup. scripts/perf/micro only has client-retained-size.ts. No streaming or GC benchmark exists
Documents a foreground `node apps/server/dist/bin.mjs serve` without the flag; scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135 prints the same hint

Node 24.21: default new_space 128 MiB; v8.setFlagsFromString('--max-semi-space-size=16') at runtime still 128 MiB; CLI flag 32 MiB. Electron 44.7 ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: default 63.5 MiB, with flag 31 MiB, so the flag is honored but the desktop baseline is half of Node's
process.execve exists on Node 24.21 (engines ^22.16||^23.11||>=24.10 all have it). A re-exec costs about 27 ms (55.7 vs 28.8 ms median) and keeps the PID, fds and TTY

remaining: 1) CLI entry: apps/server/src/bin.ts:34 does not apply the cap. Affected: foreground `ryco`, `ryco start`, `ryco serve`, `npx ryco-cli` (the README quick-start), and the Desktop's SSH-managed remote server (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:336-346 runner, launched long-lived at :469). On plain Node these run with a 128 MiB new space, the full ~50 MiB idle-RSS case. Nothing documents the flag either (README.md, REMOTE.md, apps/server/README.md:39, scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135). 2) No benchmark checks scavenge frequency, GC pause time or throughput under streaming load with the 16 MiB cap, which now ships to every packaged desktop and node service. The perf harness (scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts:78-90) can't pass node args at all. 3) Minor: a node service installed before #710 keeps its unit without the flag until `ryco service install`/setup runs again (node:update does this; a plain `npm i -g ryco-cli` upgrade does not), and nothing re-renders stale units.
fixDefects: None in the shipped code. The flag works in Electron's node mode (verified empirically) and in the units, and it never reaches provider CLIs through NODE_OPTIONS. Note on expected gain: Electron 44's default new space is about 64 MiB, not Node's 128 MiB, so the packaged-desktop saving is probably about 30 MiB rather than the ~50 MiB measured on plain Node. The code comment in backendLauncher.ts:20-22 ("128 MiB ... about 50 MiB") overstates it for Electron.
implementationSketch: A) CLI re-exec, which covers foreground ryco/start/serve, npx and the SSH remote in one place. Move the flag list into one shared constant, e.g. packages/shared/src/serverRuntimeFlags.ts (subpath export @ryco/shared/serverRuntimeFlags) exporting SERVER_V8_FLAGS = ["--max-semi-space-size=16"], and import it from apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts, apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts and the new shim so the three can't drift. Add a pure decision function, e.g. apps/server/src/serverReexec.ts: serverReexecArgs({argv, execArgv, env, versions, hasExecve}) returns string[] | null. It returns args only when all of these hold: argv[2] is undefined, starts with '-', or is 'start'/'serve' (never mcp, device-host-stdio, the stdio proxy, auth/config/service/etc.); versions.bun and versions.electron are undefined, and argv has no --bootstrap-fd; process.execve is a function (POSIX, Node >=22.15); no --max-semi-space-size in execArgv or env.NODE_OPTIONS; env.RYCO_V8_REEXEC !== '0'. In bin.ts, before enableCompileCacheBestEffort(), call it and, when non-null, run try { process.execve(process.execPath, [process.execPath, ...SERVER_V8_FLAGS, ...process.execArgv, ...process.argv.slice(1)], process.env) } catch { /* continue without the cap */ }. execve keeps the PID, fds and TTY, so launchd/systemd, the SSH PID file and Ctrl-C behave as before; services and desktop already carry the flag and skip the re-exec. Optionally also pass the flag directly in the dev branch of packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:337 (`exec node --max-semi-space-size=16 "$RYCO_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH"`). Changing the runner bytes restarts managed remote servers on the next connect (RUNNER_CHANGED), which is acceptable. Tests: unit-test serverReexecArgs over the matrix (serve/start/bare/flags-only yes; mcp/device-host/stdio-proxy/auth no; Bun/Electron/bootstrap-fd no; already flagged via execArgv or NODE_OPTIONS no; opt-out env no). Measure time-to-listening for `ryco serve` before and after (expect about +25-40 ms) and idle RSS at 5 s (expect about -50 MiB). Update apps/server/README.md:39, scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135 and REMOTE.md (one line on the cap and the opt-out, and Windows, where there is no execve). B) Benchmark: let scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts launchProductionServer accept nodeArgs (and RYCO_PERF_NODE_ARGS) so runs match the shipped setup. Add a --require preload (scripts/perf/gcStats.cjs) that records PerformanceObserver 'gc' entries by kind (count, total and p99 duration), process.cpuUsage, old-space growth and RSS, and writes them on exit. Drive streaming load by replaying a recorded provider event fixture (thousands of content deltas plus tool events) through the orchestration/WS push path; a scripted fake provider driver works too. Compare the default against 16 (and 8). Keep 16 if GC CPU rises by no more than about 2-3% and p99 event latency does not regress. 16 MiB was Node <=20's default semi-space, so expect it to pass. C) Optional: re-render stale service units on `ryco service start/restart` when the rendered definition differs from what is on disk.
decisionReason: Purely an engineering/runtime-config change on the ryco side: no E2EE/auth, hosted lifecycle, Hub protocol or deploy impact. Choosing between a ~27 ms execve re-exec and documentation only is a small engineering call the finding already anticipated ("measure first").
correction: The auditor's PARTIAL classification and evidence are accurate. They missed that the Desktop's SSH-managed remote server (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:336-346, :469) is a separate Ryco-controlled long-lived launch path without the flag. Documentation alone does not fix it; a bin.ts re-exec covers it automatically. They also missed that the perf harness (scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts:78-90) can't run with the flag. The CLI evidence line is bin.ts:34, not :36. Gain caveat: Electron 44's default new space is about 64 MiB (measured), so the already-shipped desktop part saves less than the plain-Node ~50 MiB; the CLI/SSH paths are where the full saving remains.
